newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Oct cash tax revenues flat on Sept levels.
newsitem.headline: Russian Oct cash tax revenues flat on Sept levels.

text.p: Russian cash tax revenues for the beginning of October stayed at the same low levels as in September, Economy Minister Yevgeny Yasin said on Wednesday.
Russia collected 2.2 trillion roubles in cash in the first nine days of each month, he told a news conference.
"That is not much," he said. "The budget crisis is continuing."
Tax receipts for the first nine days of October were 61 percent of the government's plan, higher than September's 50 percent, he said.
But he added that cash receipts, the most important factor for the government, were the same in both months.
Tax shortfall is one of the most serious problems in Russia, worrying the International Monetary Fund, which over the summer delayed payment of a tranches of a $10 billion loan to Russia.
On Thursday the government threatened six big companies with bankruptcy if they did not pay taxes within a week.
Last week Presdient Boris Yeltsin set up an emergency commission headed by Prime Minsiter Viktor Chernomyrdin to improve tax collection.
But Yasin said Russia was on the edge of economic turnaround. "We are poised for a very important breakthrough towards economic growth," he said.
